name: Rosso Corsa
lede: Rosso corsa is Italian for racing red: the bright red of Italian racing cars.

sections.title: Racing red
sections.body: *Rosso corsa* means "racing red" [1]. St Clair traces it to the 1907 Peking to Paris motor race, in which Prince Scipione Borghese drove an Itala painted a strident poppy red [1]. The victory made that first paint Italy's racing color, which Enzo Ferrari later took for his own cars [1]. This is a single-source account, and we have not found a second book that tells the story, so treat the exact chain of events with care.

sections.title: The race and the paint
sections.body:
Le Matin posed the challenge on 31 January 1907, and the car's journey was about 12,000 miles across the Gobi and the Urals [1]. Along the way the red faded: by Moscow the car had turned, in a companion's words, the color of the earth [1]. The fame of the red came from the finish, not from the paint as it looked on the road.

The swatch here is a plain, saturated red; real racing paints varied, and screens shift the color [2]. For its relatives see [[red]], [[vermilion]], [[scarlet]] and [[crimson]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive the swatch appears in 19 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 60% of the named colors [2]. In 95% of the 22 paintings where it covers enough canvas, it is an accent [2]. The earliest is from 1450, long before any car, so these paintings show a look-alike red, not the racing color [2].

origin.source: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour
